judge_assessment.explanation: The hard failure is exact and I confirmed it by reading final_response.md end to end: it opens 'Three documents, all compiled and gated: a 10-problem student worksheet, a full step-by-step answer key, and a 2-page study guide' and never names a file. There is no 'ws_', 'ak_' or 'ss_' filename and no path anywhere in the response -- and every other case I reviewed in this shard (curr-002, 013, 019, 025, 026, 038, 044) names all three PDFs explicitly, so this is a lapse, not a house style. The age-fit and page-flow error is also right: pdfinfo gives 5 pages, page 5 holds only problem 10, and problems 1, 2, 5, 6, 8 and 10 carry no figure at all, so a five-year-old must hold 'two identical right triangles ... their longest sides touch exactly' in their head. Where I go further than the judge: problem 6's keyed answer is not unique. Two congruent right triangles joined along the hypotenuse give a rectangle when one is rotated 180 degrees about the hypotenuse midpoint, but a kite when one is reflected across the hypotenuse -- both satisfy 'longest sides touch exactly' -- and the key states 'The shape is a rectangle' flatly, which would mark a correct kite build wrong. The judge's 'all manual items have plausible keyed criteria' does not hold for problem 6. Everything else recomputes: 8, 6, '>', 12, '<', 12, and the order 2, 3, 6.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 10 is a well-judged synthesis item for this age: one hexagon covered three ways (2 trapezoids, 3 rhombuses, 6 triangles), ordered fewest to most, and the key lands the inverse relation explicitly -- 'the pieces get smaller as you go down that list, and the count gets bigger.' That is the idea the whole sheet exists to build.

Problems 3, 6 and 9 are correctly declared {"type": "manual"} with substantive descs, and the build exits 2 rather than inventing checks for drawings. On a geometry-construction sheet that is the honest encoding, and it is the opposite failure mode from the rest of this shard.

The two declared traps are the right ones for equal-group counting: 7 on problem 5 (adding 3 and 4 instead of making four groups of three) and 6 on problem 8 (stopping after the first hexagon). Both are machine-checked as distinguishable and both print in the key.
The pattern-block name key sits with the directions as a value-free figure, so piece vocabulary is shared once without any figure carrying a count into a problem.

root_causes.description: SKILL.md's Deliver step tells the agent to 'report the three output paths clearly' but no gate checks that the response actually did. The scoring harness has a detector (response_surfaces() in scripts/score_eval_run.py, which raises 'artifact_not_surfaced') -- it just runs after the fact, on the judging side, instead of inside build.sh where the author could act on it.
evidence: final_response.md contains no filename or path for any of the three PDFs
SKILL.md section 6 'Deliver' has no must-name-the-files requirement
every other case in this shard names ws_/ak_/ss_ filenames

root_causes.description: Problem 6's keyed answer is not the unique correct build, and the study guide's Skill 2 worked example is worksheet problem 6 with the answer supplied, so a child reading the guide first copies the answer to one of the three manual items.
evidence: worksheet problem 6: 'Two identical right triangles are put together so that their longest sides touch exactly. Draw the shape they make and write its name.'
answer_key.pdf problem 6: 'The shape is a rectangle.' -- but reflecting one triangle across the hypotenuse also makes their longest sides touch exactly and yields a kite, not a rectangle
study_guide.pdf Skill 2 Example: 'Two identical right triangles are joined so that their longest sides touch exactly. Name the new shape.' => 'rectangle'

root_causes.description: A K-1 geometry sheet on composing shapes was written almost entirely in prose. Six of ten problems carry no figure, and the ones that need a build the most (problems 6 and 9) describe it in words using 'right triangle' and 'longest side' -- vocabulary well beyond K.G / 1.G. The result is 5 pages with a single problem on the last.
evidence: pdfinfo worksheet.pdf -> Pages: 5; page 5 holds only problem 10
official dimension scores: clarity_and_accessibility 2, visual_and_print_quality 2 -- the lowest pair in the shard

improvements.title: The delivery response must name and link all three PDFs
improvements.proposed_change: Make artifact surfacing a build-time obligation rather than a post-hoc scoring observation. (a) In SKILL.md section 6, state that the response MUST name each of the three files (worksheet, answer key, study guide) by its ws_/ak_/ss_ filename or full path -- 'three documents are ready' is not delivery. (b) Have build.sh print a ready-to-paste delivery block containing the three filenames next to the existing PDF path list, so the correct text is in front of the agent at the moment it writes the response. Reuse the matching logic already implemented in response_surfaces() so the build-time rule and the scoring rule cannot drift.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_scoring_harness.py, add a case whose final_response.md reads 'Three documents are ready: a worksheet, an answer key and a study guide.' with all three PDFs present, and assert an artifact_not_surfaced error is raised for each of the three roles. Pair it with a build.sh test asserting the gate summary emits the three filenames.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the sole hard failure on this case and the whole artifact_not_surfaced class -- a defect that costs a REJECT even when the material is correct, as it did here (23/32 with correct mathematics).
improvements.risk: Low. Additive build output plus a documentation rule; no change to any mathematical or layout gate.

improvements.title: Problem 6's key names one build when two satisfy the wording
improvements.proposed_change: Either tighten the stem or widen the key. Tighter stem: 'Two identical right triangles are put together so that their longest sides touch and the two square corners end up at opposite ends.' Wider key: state that a rectangle results when one triangle is turned halfway around, and a kite when it is flipped over the long side, and credit both. Also fold the alternative into the manual desc in verify.json so the grading criterion travels with the check. Same treatment for the study guide's Skill 2 example, which repeats the claim.
improvements.regression_test: Add this item to the manual-review-aid corpus with both builds as acceptable answers, and assert the reviewer flags a key that admits only one. The current key text names only 'rectangle', so the check fails before the wording is fixed.
improvements.expected_impact: A child who correctly flips one triangle instead of rotating it stops being marked wrong on a manual item, and the answer key stops asserting a false uniqueness.
improvements.risk: Low, but the wider key must stay readable for a K-1 adult -- prefer the tightened stem, which removes the ambiguity instead of explaining it.

improvements.title: The Skill 2 worked example is worksheet problem 6 with its answer given
improvements.proposed_change: Add a gate: for every study-guide example and try-it, compare its stem against each worksheet problem stem and fail when the overlap is near-identical. The study guide is explicitly 'for use while completing your worksheet', so an example that duplicates a worksheet item hands over the answer -- worst of all here, where problem 6 is one of the three manual items an adult is meant to assess. tests/check_ss_coverage.py already reads both documents and is the natural home.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture pair where the study guide's example stem and a worksheet problem stem share most of their content words; assert check_ss_coverage.py fails naming the duplicated problem. It passes today -- this case shipped with the duplicate.
improvements.expected_impact: The study guide teaches the method on a parallel item rather than pre-answering a graded one. It also protects the coverage gate's intent, which is that the guide covers every tested SKILL, not every tested PROBLEM.
improvements.risk: Medium: a topic with few natural instances will trip a naive similarity threshold. Compare numeric givens as well as wording, and only fail when both the structure and the numbers match.

improvements.title: K-1 shape-composition items must be drawn, not described
improvements.proposed_change: For the foundations-k1 band on geometry topics, require a figure for any item whose stem names a shape relationship the child must build ('put together so that', 'covered by', 'joined so that'). Problems 1, 2, 5, 6, 8 and 10 here are pure prose. Route them through scripts/render_figures.py / \probfig so the pieces are shown, and drop the adult vocabulary ('right triangle', 'longest side') in favour of the drawn piece. Extend tests/check_layout.py's existing figure-scope rules with a band-aware requirement.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a foundations-k1 geometry worksheet whose problem prose contains 'put together so that' and which declares no \probfig for that id; assert check_layout.py reports the missing figure. No such check exists today.
improvements.expected_impact: Directly addresses the two lowest dimension scores on this case (clarity_and_accessibility 2, visual_and_print_quality 2). Drawing the builds also shortens the prose enough to pull problem 10 off its own page, fixing the 5-page/orphan-page complaint at the same time.
improvements.risk: Medium: more figures means more page area, so pair it with a workspace reduction or the sheet grows instead of shrinking. Validate against the compile-ws page budget.

improvements.title: Quick Answers bank prints an em-dash instead of the verified > / < relation
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, _fmt() sends every string 'expected' through sympy.sympify(); '>' and '<' raise SympifyError and fall through to the '---' branch, which the module's own docstring reserves for 'see solution' / manual-only ids. Add a relation branch before the sympify attempt: map the bare relation tokens ('>', '<', '>=', '<=', '=', '≥', '≤') to their math-mode LaTeX ($>$, $<$, $\ge$, $\le$, $=$) and return that. Everything else keeps its current behaviour, so genuinely manual ids still print '---' and remain distinguishable from a verified relation.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py that renders a verify JSON containing {"id": 1, "type": "compare", "values": ["5+3", "4+2"], "order": "relation", "expected": ">"} alongside a {"id": 2, "type": "manual"} entry, and asserts the bank line for id 1 contains '$>$' while the line for id 2 is '---'. It fails today because both render '---'.
improvements.expected_impact: Every worksheet whose verification_targets include 'compare' with order 'relation' regains real entries in the grader's at-a-glance bank. In this shard alone that is curr-002 (2 of 10 entries), curr-006 (2 of 8), curr-032 (2 of 10), curr-038 (part of entry 8) and curr-050 (2 of 10).
improvements.risk: Low and contained to the bank. The entries are plain text by design and are never read by check_answer_key.py, so the strict per-problem binding gate cannot be affected. Only risk is choosing a LaTeX spelling that does not compile, which the existing compile-ak gate would catch immediately.

case_summary: The shape-composition mathematics is correct -- 8 tiles, 6 triangles, 6 > 3, 12 triangles, 8 < 16, 12 triangles, and the ordering 2, 3, 6 all recompute -- and problems 3, 6 and 9 are honestly declared manual with the build exiting 2, which is the right instinct and the opposite of this shard's usual failure. It is rejected because final_response.md never names a single file: it says 'three documents, all compiled and gated' and stops, so nothing is actually delivered to the user. Beyond that, the sheet is the weakest-presented in my shard -- six of ten problems have no figure at all on a K-1 GEOMETRY sheet about composing shapes, the stems lean on 'right triangle' and 'longest side', and five pages end with problem 10 alone. Two findings the judge did not raise: problem 6's keyed 'rectangle' is not the unique build (flipping one triangle across the hypotenuse gives a kite and equally satisfies 'longest sides touch exactly'), and the study guide's Skill 2 worked example is worksheet problem 6 with the answer supplied, which pre-answers one of the three manual items.
